name: Nuwara Eliya
title: Nuwara Eliya guide — Horton Plains, tea, where to stay | Ceylon Hop
description: What to do in Nuwara Eliya — Horton Plains at dawn, the tea estates, what to wear, where to eat and stay, and how we drive you up the hill.

hero.intro: Mornings are misty, nights are cold, and it feels nothing like the coast. A hill-country town at 1,868 m, ringed by tea — the British called it Little England and built it to match.

lede: Most people stay two nights, usually on their way between Kandy and Ella —
ledeEm: one day for Horton Plains, one for the town and tea.

gettingHere.heading: We’ll bring you up the hill
gettingHere.sub: Hotel to hotel, fixed price, one driver who knows the road. From wherever you are.

origins.title: From Kandy
origins.from: 75 km · 2 h 45 · most people arrive from here
origins.sell: The A5 is 60 km of hairpins after Gampola. Our drivers do it every week — no overtaking on the bends, a stop at Ramboda Falls, and they know which roadside stall has the good strawberries.

origins.title: From Ella
origins.from: 55 km · 1 h 45 · the return leg of the loop
origins.sell: Up through the Ella Gap with the southern plain opening below you, past Hakgala gardens, then tea all the way. We can stop at the gardens on the way in if you’d like.

origins.title: Straight from the airport
origins.from: CMB · 170 km · about 5 h 30 with a lunch stop
origins.sell: Your driver meets you at arrivals with your name; you sleep in the hills that night. The easiest way to start a trip if you want the cool air first and the beaches last.

gettingHere.train: It’s a beautiful ride and we’ll never tell you not to. Two things to know: the line stops at Nanu Oya, 9 km from town, so you still need a ride at the end; and reserved seats go on sale 30 days ahead and sell out in season (the unreserved carriages always have room if you don’t mind standing). From Kandy it’s about 4 h, from Ella about 3 h. Message us and we’ll check seats for your date — and tell you which side to sit on.

places.name: Horton Plains & World’s End
places.text: A high plateau with a 9.5 km walking loop that leads to World’s End — a cliff with a drop of around 880 m — and Baker’s Falls. It is not near town: 32 km and about an hour on a narrow mountain road, which is why the early start matters.

spec.open: Gate opens 6 AM · last entry mid-afternoon
spec.ticket: ≈ Rs 7,000 foreign adult · pay at the gate

tip.text: Go first thing in the morning. By mid-morning the mist usually rolls in and the view disappears. No phone signal on the plains — download the map before you leave the hotel. Leave the hotel by 5:30 and you’ll be at World’s End before the tour buses. Bring a jumper you can take off — it’s 8° at the gate and 20° by ten.

offer.title: 5:30 AM pickup with Ceylon Hop
offer.sub: Wait at the park and the drive back included
offer.wa: Hi Ceylon Hop — I’m reading your Nuwara Eliya guide. Could you give me a price for a 5:30 AM Horton Plains pickup from my hotel, with the wait and the drive back?

places.name: Pedro Tea Estate
places.text: A working tea estate 3 km from town. A short tour shows you withering, rolling and firing, then you get a cup in the café over the bushes it came from.

spec.open: Tours Mon–Sat, mornings · factory idle Sun

tip.text: Go in the morning while the machines are running — an idle factory is just a big shed. Lover’s Leap waterfall is a 20-minute walk up from the estate gate and free.

places.name: Gregory Lake
places.text: The lake in the middle of town. It’s nice for a slow walk in the morning or late afternoon; the full loop is about 4 km and flat.

spec.from: In town · walk from most hotels
spec.open: Open all day · small entry fee to the lakeside park

tip.text: If you fancy a boat or horse ride, agree on the price first. It isn’t fixed, and some visitors felt short rides weren’t great value.

places.name: Hakgala Botanical Garden
places.text: A cool, shady botanical garden on the road to Ella — ferns, roses, an orchid house and a lot of monkeys. Easy walking, good for families and for the day after Horton Plains.

spec.from: 10 km · 20 min, on the Ella road

tip.text: If you’re leaving for Ella, we stop here on the way out — no need to come back for it.

places.name: Victoria Park & the old town
places.text: A neat Victorian park next to the red-brick post office, with the racecourse and the golf course beyond it. Birdwatchers come for the hill-country species; everyone else comes in April when the flower beds peak. Give the town itself an hour: the covered market for strawberries and vegetables, the post office, a look at the Hill Club from the road.

spec.open: Park opens 7 AM · small entry fee

places.name: Single Tree Hill at sunrise
places.text: The viewpoint above town. A steep 40-minute walk up through tea from the Haddon Hill road, and the whole valley below you as the mist burns off. The morning you’re not doing Horton Plains, do this.

spec.from: 2 km · start on foot from town

places.name: Moon Plains
places.text: The gentle alternative to Horton Plains: a grassland plateau 15 minutes from town with a jeep ride to a 360° viewpoint and, on a clear day, Adam’s Peak on the horizon. Sambar deer most mornings.

spec.open: Opens 7 AM · jeep included in the ticket

tip.text: Can’t face the 5:30 start, or travelling with small children? This gives you the plains feeling without the long road.

places.name: Ambewela farms
places.text: Dairy country on the way to Horton Plains — black-and-white cows, wide green paddocks and a farm shop with fresh milk, yoghurt and cheese. Locals call it Little New Zealand. Children love it; adults like the yoghurt.

spec.from: 20 km · on the Horton Plains road
spec.open: Open daily, daytime · small entry fee

tip.text: The easy add-on to a Horton Plains morning — you pass the gate on the way back down.

places.name: Lover’s Leap waterfall
places.text: A 30 m fall above the Pedro estate with a legend attached (a prince, a village girl, a leap). The walk up from the estate is 20 minutes through tea, the pool at the bottom is cold, and it costs nothing.

spec.from: 4 km · walk up from Pedro estate

furtherAfield.name: Adam’s Peak (Sri Pada)
furtherAfield.text: The night climb to the summit for sunrise: 5,500 steps, pilgrims all the way up. Season is December to May; outside it the path is dark and the tea shops shut. We drive you to Dalhousie the evening before.

furtherAfield.name: Lipton’s Seat & Haputale
furtherAfield.text: Where Sir Thomas Lipton looked at his tea. A tuk-tuk up through the Dambatenne estate, five provinces in view on a clear morning. Combine with the road to Ella.

furtherAfield.name: Ramboda & the tea-country waterfalls
furtherAfield.text: Ramboda, Devon and St Clair’s, all on or just off the Kandy road — the reason to do that drive in daylight rather than by night bus.

itinerary.heading: A plan that works
itinerary.sub: The order matters here: mist by mid-morning, factories closed on Sundays, cold after dark.

steps.title: Pickup from your hotel
steps.text: It’s cold. Jacket, water, no plastic bags.

steps.title: Horton Plains loop
steps.text: World’s End first while it’s clear, then Baker’s Falls. 3–4 h.

steps.title: Pedro Tea Estate
steps.text: Factory running, tea in the café after.

steps.title: Gregory Lake
steps.text: Slow walk, agree any boat price first.

steps.title: Dinner at The Hill Club
steps.text: Smart dress code. Ask for extra blankets at the hotel.

days.title: Day 2 · Town, gardens, onward
days.sub: Unhurried, then the road to Ella

steps.title: Victoria Park & the post office
steps.text: Cash from the ATMs in town while you’re here.

steps.title: Onward to Ella with us
steps.text: 1 h 45 by car, past Hakgala and down through the Ella Gap with the whole southern plain opening up below you. Or the 3 h train from Nanu Oya, if you have a seat.

months.heading: The weather, month by month
months.sub: Two monsoons hit the hill country from opposite sides, so the town has two wet seasons and one long clear one. Views are never guaranteed, but the odds change a lot.

blocks.label: Dec – Feb
blocks.title: Clear & cold
blocks.text: The best odds of a view at World’s End. Nights can touch 5°; hotels sell out over Christmas.

blocks.label: Mar – Apr
blocks.title: Season
blocks.text: Flower shows, the races, Sinhala & Tamil New Year in April. Warm days, busy town — book everything early.

blocks.label: May – Sep
blocks.title: South-west monsoon
blocks.text: Rain and mist on the western slopes, often clearing by afternoon. Fewer people, greener tea, cheaper rooms.

blocks.label: Oct – Nov
blocks.title: Showers
blocks.text: The wettest weeks: afternoon storms most days. Mornings are still your friend. Leech socks for the plains.

onTheWay.heading: Worth stopping for
onTheWay.sub: These are on the way, not in town. Your driver can stop — just ask.
onTheWay.note: Stops are free on a Ceylon Hop transfer — the link opens WhatsApp with the stop already typed, and we tell the driver.

stops.name: Seetha Amman Temple & Ramboda Falls
stops.text: A temple linked to the Ramayana, with a tall waterfall nearby. Cover shoulders and knees; shoes off at the temple.
stops.wa: Hi Ceylon Hop — on my Kandy → Nuwara Eliya transfer, could we stop at Ramboda Falls and Seetha Amman Temple? (From your Nuwara Eliya guide.)

stops.name: Strawberry & veggie stalls
stops.text: The hill country grows strawberries, carrots and leeks. Stalls sell them fresh along the road — great for snacks.
stops.wa: Hi Ceylon Hop — on my Kandy → Nuwara Eliya transfer, could we stop at a roadside strawberry stall? (From your Nuwara Eliya guide.)

eat.name: The Hill Club
eat.text: Old-style dining in a 19th-century club — five courses, a fire in the grate. Smart dress code: jacket for men, and they lend one.

eat.name: Pedro Tea Estate café
eat.text: A cup of the estate’s own tea looking over the bushes it came from. Go after the factory tour, before the mist.

eat.name: Rice & curry by the bus stand
eat.text: The lunch places around the bus stand and the market do a plate of rice, dhal and four curries for a few hundred rupees, 11:30 to about 2. This is where our drivers eat. Ask for it “not too spicy” if you mean it.

eatCollector.title: Where did you eat well?
eatCollector.text: Tell us your favourite place in Nuwara Eliya and we’ll check it out for the next traveller.
eatCollector.fine: A photo of the menu is even better.
eatCollector.wa: Hi Ceylon Hop — a place I ate well in Nuwara Eliya:

stay.name: Heritance Tea Factory
stay.text: A real 1930s tea factory turned hotel, 15 min above town, tea bushes to the door. The one people talk about afterwards.

stay.name: The Grand Hotel · Jetwing St Andrew’s
stay.text: The two colonial classics in town — lawns, afternoon tea, walking distance to the lake and the park. Grand is bigger; St Andrew’s is quieter.

stay.name: Guesthouses around Gregory Lake
stay.text: The family-run places on the lake road and up Haddon Hill are where most of our customers stay: $30–60 a night with breakfast, hot water, and owners who’ll book your Horton Plains driver at reception. Ask for a room with a heater or a fireplace — it’s worth the extra. Travelling solo? There are two or three decent hostels in the centre — message us and we’ll say which.

stayCollector.title: Stayed somewhere great?
stayCollector.text: Guesthouse, hostel, homestay — tell us and we’ll add the good ones here.
stayCollector.wa: Hi Ceylon Hop — a place I stayed and liked in Nuwara Eliya:

items.a: If you like cool air, tea country and a morning on the plains — yes, and it breaks the Kandy–Ella journey in the right place. If you want beaches, nightlife or a warm swim, this isn’t that. The town itself is a half-day; the country around it is the point.

items.q: How many days do I need?
items.a: Two nights. One morning for Horton Plains, one for the town and a tea estate. A single night works if you skip the plains; three if you want Adam’s Peak or a slow day.

items.q: When is the best time to visit?
items.a: December to April for clear mornings; April is the busiest and the most fun. May to November is wetter but quieter and cheaper — mornings are usually still fine. Month by month ↑

items.q: Can I do it as a day trip from Kandy?
items.a: You can, but it’s five and a half hours of driving for a few hours in town, and you miss the one thing worth coming for — the plains at dawn. Stay the night.

items.q: Does the train go into Nuwara Eliya?
items.a:
Not quite. The train stops at Nanu Oya, about 9 km from town, so you’ll still need a ride for the last stretch.

If you’d rather skip the change, we do the whole trip from Kandy hotel to hotel, and stop at Ramboda Falls on the way. See how we get you here ↑
From Kandy, take the train to Nanu Oya. To carry on to Ella, take Nanu Oya → Ella — one of the prettiest stretches on the whole line.

items.q: Can I go from Kandy to Ella in one day?
items.a: You can, but it’s a very long day. Stopping in Nuwara Eliya makes it much easier.

items.q: Are train tickets easy to get?
items.a: Reserved seats go on sale 30 days ahead and sell out fast in season. If they’re gone, the unreserved second-class carriages always have space — you may stand for part of it, and it’s the same view. Message us on WhatsApp and we’ll check what’s left for your date.

items.q: What if the train is delayed or cancelled?
items.a: It happens, especially in heavy rain. Don’t plan anything tight on the same day.

items.q: How cold does it really get?
items.a:
18–24°Day
10–14°Night
8–10°Dawn
ColderHorton

Mist and rain can show up any time, which makes it feel colder than the number says.

• Layers: t-shirt, jumper, jacket
  • Long trousers
  • A rain jacket
  • Closed shoes with grip

items.q: What should I bring for Horton Plains?
items.a: A warm layer for the early start, a rain jacket, sunscreen and water. Plastic bags aren’t allowed in the park.
Many places don’t. Ask for extra blankets when you check in, or pick a room with a fireplace — the guesthouses here charge a little more for them and it’s worth it in December.

items.q: What if I get ill or hurt up here?
items.a: There are pharmacies along the main street and a district general hospital in town. Altitude and cold catch people out more than anything else — drink water, take the first day slowly.

tips: Carry some cash. Tea factories, stalls and small shops are often cash-only. The bank ATMs are around the post office — and they can run dry on long weekends, so don’t arrive with nothing.
Tuk-tuk fares aren’t metered. Agree the price first: a few hundred rupees across town, more to the tea estates, and a proper negotiation for Horton Plains. Your hotel will tell you what’s fair today.
No phone signal on Horton Plains and patchy on the Kandy road. Download your map and this page before you set off.
The Hill Club means it about the dress code — jacket and tie for men at dinner (they lend both), no trainers. Ask the day before.
If someone says a place is “closed today” and offers another, check with us first — it usually isn’t.
Leeches in the wet months at Horton Plains. Long socks, or buy leech socks at the gate.
The roads are twisty. If you get car sick, take a tablet before the drive up.
April is busy — flower shows, horse races, New Year travel. Book early.
Full-moon (Poya) days: alcohol isn’t sold, the temples are packed and some places close early. Check the date before you plan a big dinner.
Views aren’t guaranteed. The mist comes and goes.

ask.heading: Not sure about something?
ask.text: Train seats, factory opening days, what the entrance fee is this month — message us and we’ll check. That’s what we’re here for.
